- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) or shows recent reversal, model often overpredicts downward moves; adjust downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops after peak or rises after trough), model tends to lag; add 1–2 day lag correction to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates long-term upward trends; increase forecast by 2–5% if sentiment is bullish and price has been trending up for 5+ days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, model often fails to catch the momentum; adjust forecast upward by 2–4% for next 5 days.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment confirms strong directional shift (e.g., >2 consecutive +1.00 sentiment); otherwise, model overreacts and underperforms.
